main_text.l: sint, tibi donare, dicarem. Munus est Leuiden-
sæ crasso filo factum, si me meáque consideres.
Sin spectes res à me aliunde mutuò sumptas,
& velut in lancem Satyram promiscuè con-
gestas, oculis tuis fortasse non indignum. Illud
ita tibi gratum & acceptum sit exopto, ut non
displiceat ulli eorum, quos habet bonos &
doctos innumerabiles Britannia magna. Fœlix, si
sua bona norit: fœlicior, si iisdem bene utatur
notis: fœlicissima, si eadem perpetuò ad finem
usque Deo bene favente retineat & conser-
vet. Habet illa φιλοσόφους, in omni genere
πολιτείας dextros & peritos gubernatores, propè
infinitos. Sed præ omnibus & supra o-
mneis eximium θεόφρον Regem serenissi-
mum, potentissimum & doctissimum, ῥητῶρα
λόγων, ϖρακτῆρα τῶν ἔργων. Illi à supremo Regum
rege fausta omnia ardentissimis votis pre-
camur omnes, qui hîc sumus pij. Omnibus
ipsius Maiestati subditis populis sanctam
& constantem in vera pietate Euangelica con-

page.notes: Greek words in the text (φιλοσόφους, πολιτείας, θεόφρον, ῥητῶρα, λόγων, ϖρακτῆρα, τῶν ἔργων) are transcribed as best read; the Greek on the scan is small and partly blurred, so accents and some letters are uncertain. The line "sint, tibi donare" begins as a fragment. The "iiij" signature is printed beside an asterisk at the foot and is treated as a signature.
